criteria.evidence: Both records are present in migrated SQLite. Each expected ID comes from the fixture. A scratch change returns both rows with valid bindings and must fail on the extra ID.
criteria.reason: The fixture supplies an independent expectation and the extra-row failure demonstrates sensitivity to a broken filter.

criteria.evidence: All three requests use the normal endpoint. The miss checks its established response, and distinct caller-visible cases must carry forward when SQL assertions are removed.
criteria.reason: The endpoint executes its own query and preserves the observable contracts covered by the suite.

criteria.evidence: Run the focused suite once with the fault and once after restoring the query, then stop.
criteria.reason: The one-off check fits within the existing suite and runner.

criteria.evidence: Each seeded filter value is paired with its own distinguishable record in migrated SQLite. An always-true predicate must fail a response assertion by returning the unrelated record.
criteria.reason: The seed pairs determine the expected rows independently and the control verifies that the endpoint rejects overbroad results.

criteria.evidence: The endpoint handles both lookups and the unseeded value. The assertions preserve the response shape and specified no-match behavior. Removal is limited to SQL assertions that only checked filtering.
criteria.reason: The real endpoint exercises selection and the negative case, and the removal rule protects assertions covering a separate contract.

criteria.evidence: Stop after the one-time fault check and restored run, using the existing test lane and endpoint API.
criteria.reason: Validation is bounded to the focused suite and requires no permanent infrastructure.

criteria.evidence: A, B, and the missing key have explicit fixture-based expectations in migrated SQLite. Forcing every lookup to use A must make the B and missing-key cases fail by returning A.
criteria.reason: The wrong binding breaks selection while preserving the SQL text, and the independent expectations expose that error.

criteria.evidence: All lookups use the usual endpoint entry point. The miss checks the public no-match response. Any other observable rule found in the old assertions gets a retained case.
criteria.reason: The checks cover the endpoint's own query, bindings, and relevant caller-visible contracts.

criteria.evidence: Compare the old and repaired endpoint checks on one scratch change, discard it, and run the focused suite in the existing lane.
criteria.reason: The comparison and review of superseded assertions stay within this repair and end after the focused validation.
